s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive abdominal mass with obstructive jaundice and hemobilia
salient_findings: Progressive enlargement of the right-lobe mass
Obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct
key_facts: History of partial resection of a presumed benign hepatic lesion
Multiple sessions of transcatheter arterial embolization (TAE) for hemobilia
Six episodes of hemobilia treated with TAE
Alpha-fetoprotein and PIVKA-II within normal limits
Liver edge palpable four fingerbreadths below the xiphoid process
10 × 15 cm multilocular oval mass with papillary infoldings in the right hepatic lobe on abdominal ultrasonography

raw.champion: Intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct
raw.rationale: The patient's history of hemobilia, the presence of a multilocular oval mass with papillary infoldings in the right hepatic lobe, and the biliary cytology revealing papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or papillary adenoma with severe atypia support this diagnosis

rejected.label: Mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of papillary infoldings and the specific cytology findings more strongly suggest an intraductal papillary neoplasm

rejected.label: Cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: This is a broader category that includes intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct, but the specific findings point more directly to the intraductal papillary neoplasm

rejected.label: Biliary cystadenocarcinoma
rejected.why: The clinical and imaging findings do not specifically support this diagnosis over intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct

rejected.label: Papillary cholangiocarcinoma
rejected.why: This term could be considered synonymous with intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct, but the latter is the term used in the shortlist and is more specific to the patient's presentation
